newsitem.title: GERMANY: Four guilty in Berlin Kurdish-Iranian murders.
newsitem.headline: Four guilty in Berlin Kurdish-Iranian murders.

text.p: A Berlin court on Thursday handed down life sentences to the two suspects in the assassination of a group of dissident Iranian Kurdish leaders in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in 1992.

Presiding judge Frithjof Kubsch gave long sentences to two other suspects and found a fifth innocent of the murder of Sadegh Sharafkandi, exiled leader of the Iranian Democratic Party of Kurdistan, and two fellow officials and a translator.
It was not immediately clear whether Kubsch would directly attribute blame for the attack either to Iran in general or to specific leaders.

Prosecutors in the trial infuriated Tehran and strained bilateral relations by alleging that Iran's supreme religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei ordered the killings and President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani approved them. Germany has already issued an arrest warrant for Iranian Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan.
The Islamic state denies all responsibility for the killings, and various politicians and religious leaders have accused Germany of orchestrating a political trial.
Kubsch gave life sentences to Kazem Darabi, an Iranian, and Abbas Rhayel, a Lebanese. Two other Lebanese got prison sentences of between five and 11 years as accomplices.
